reason: The hypothesis directly restates the finding from P1 and P3 that thermal exposure of FeCoNiMnCu HEA coating on steel at 800 °C forms a protective Cr2O3 layer that enhances wear resistance, proposing the same intervention (pre-oxidation) and mechanism for the same alloy system, with only a minor change from Mn to Cr in the alloy composition and a slight broadening of the temperature range. The core idea, mechanism, and predicted outcome are all taken from a single source (P1/P3), making it a restatement of a reported result as a prediction.

high-temperature wear resistance improvement via oxide layer
mechanism of oxide layer reducing metallic contact and wear
